summary:
The guard now accounts for every leaf a provider declares, in all nine ported languages, and its forms read all twenty runtimes. I changed no file under ts/src or ts/project, and ts/dist is unchanged.

**What I ran:**
- Guard: 39/39. Reader: 22/22 (20 languages, plus the forms-count test and the table test).
- Suite without the toolchain lanes: 2586 tests, 2581 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.
- `git status` is clean after a full `npm run build`.
- The check's 52 mutations plus my 19, each rebuilt: 62 of 71 caught.
  - Of the check's 52: 43 caught (it reported 27).
  - Of mine: 19 of 19 caught.
  - Every miss is in a stated category. All nine misses are the check's own: one return compared with nothing (clojure), one convention noun, two literals (language), two type printers with no column, one c type exception, two printer internals.

**What changed in the guard:**
- Each operation's method is the one its own source defines. The default is the `Entity<Op>Op` fragment; c uses the vtable order; ocaml uses the record field.
- Parameter names and types are compared, with declared renames and type names, each with a reason.
- A member is looked up only on the object that has it.
- The record printer must call the record accessor.
- A comparison that compares nothing is counted and needs a reason.
- A type printer with no column needs a reason.
- A compiled forms file with no source fails.
- An entity accessor's argument is derived from the entity constructor it is passed to.
- A citation is checked: the file belongs to the runtime, the quote is still there, and the value's code tokens are in the quote. Where no quote can hold the value (prose, a boolean, a member kind, a note), the citation pins the value it audited.

**Found on the way (read, then confirmed by the guard):**
- The handed guard's undocumented-member check had never fired in any language. The literal `{ctor}` in its known-names list became the wildcard `\w+`.
- Six declared facts are wrong (rust has one in a note), in six languages:
  - ts, go, py, rb, clojure: `accessor.arg: 'data'`, so the page says "Pass … for no initial data". Each runtime forwards the argument to the entity constructor's `entopts`.
  - py: `data_set` and `match_set` show a keyword (`data=`/`match=`) the runtime does not have; it names it `args`.
  - rust: the direct note says `Err` is "reserved for a request that could not be made". `direct` never returns `Err`.

  All are recorded as `WRONG:` exceptions for the next engineer.

**H1:**
- A language supplies one forms file, about 45 to 105 lines.
- The framework grew additively: `declReader`, file parts (`path#from#to`), a return read from a later line, `absentOps`, `param`, `renames`, `typeNames`, `uncompared`, `cite`, value pins. These let it read perl's `my (...) = @_`, ocaml's arrows and record fields, java's overloads, kotlin/scala/swift properties, swift's next-line returns, lua's `---@return` pairs and cpp's class sections.
- Measured against the handed state, the only change that forced edits in existing forms files was making the new account pass: citations and parameter readers had to be added. That is new required content, not a changed interface.
- No shared file needs a per-language edit to port one of the eleven. The one exception would be a fact key with no default category, which fails loudly.

The reader cannot see C++ access sections: cpp's private/protected members appear as public and carry reasons instead.
Notes are cited as prose and pinned. Their backticked tokens (go `StreamItem`, `callopts["ctrl"]`) are not checked against the quote.
I did not run any toolchain lane or the golden test per mutation, only the guard and the reader. I did not check whether the golden hash test would also fail on each provider mutation.
The comment gate exits 1 on the handed tree. My files are clean (its total went from 27 to 22 findings; the rest are in other files, not mine).
Parameter-name renames and typeNames are declared by the same porter who writes the provider; they are listed with a reason, not independently checked.
I did not fix any provider (not mine): the WRONG facts stand in the providers.
The 52 mutations ran against a copy of my clone (2a87287f plus my commits), not the check's v3-frozen clone. One mutation's 'from' text was adjusted to my changed forms (forms-vacuous-ts).
surprises: The handed guard's 'public member neither declared nor undocumented' check never fired in any language. The known-names list contained the literal '{ctor}', and namePattern turned it into \w+, which matched every name. The handed negative controls passed through the family check instead.

Five of nine ported providers (ts, go, py, rb, clojure) tell the reader the accessor takes initial data. Every runtime passes the argument to the entity constructor as entopts. ts's own component says so in a comment.
